correctness.rationale: For positive binary-palindrome numerator and denominator all values are odd. At fixed k=14, if odd N with leading block t and last block r has a palindrome-denominator B with >=14 bits, the forced numerator prefix a=rev_14(r rev_14(b) mod 2^14) and product-leading-block interval condition (2) must hold for some 14-bit b. Exhaustive integer enumeration of failing (t,r) gives T=45,362,298, and each prefix-boundary q=0..8192 has minimal forced nonrepresentable odd density 80,469,557/240,599,040 at q=6493. The independently compiled and executed C++ enumeration recomputed all widths 3..14 and the exact k=14 minimum; independent direct brute force at k3..7 matched obstruction counts. Binary-palindromic denominators shorter than 14 bits form a finite collection, each with O(sqrt X) possible numerator palindromes up to BX, giving zero density. Adding disjoint even integers of density 1/2 yields lower nonrepresentable density 200,769,077/240,599,040 and hence representable upper density 39,829,963/240,599,040<1/6. Exact proof uses length-shell equidistribution of prefix/suffix cylinders; finite search is exhaustive ONLY at chosen width, not a proof of conjectured density zero.
